walkthroughs.body_html:
What is Business? — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

What is Business? brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with What is Business?.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Porter's three generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
options: Diversification
Focus
Innovation
Acquisition

mcqs.q: The 'Blue Ocean' concept was proposed by:
options: Porter
Kim and Mauborgne
Hamel and Prahalad
Drucker

mcqs.q: How do stakeholder and shareholder interests overlap and conflict?
options: Stakeholders and shareholders always want the same thing.
Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.

Shareholders are a subset of stakeholders. Their interests overlap (long-term success benefits all) but conflict on issues like dividends vs investment, wages vs profits, or short-term gains vs long-term sustainability.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
Shareholders' personal assets are protected if the company fails — they can only lose the amount they invested, not their personal wealth.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
Limited liability means the company has limited debts it can take on.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
Shareholders are external and stakeholders are internal.
People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.
The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
